synthesis.body: Adding a schema, a validator call, or a test is not the same as adding a gate. Five distinct instances in one change, each of which reported green while checking nothing: (1) contracts/plugin-manifest.derived.schema.json described a plugin `source` object, but build/main.py pops `source` before validate_derived_plugin_manifest_dict, so it never saw one — proven by every live marketplace entry carrying `category`, which that schema forbids; (2) a new verify.py check placed the root-marketplace validation below an `if not dist_dir.exists(): return []` early return, making it unreachable in CI, where dist/ is gitignored and never built; (3) both schemas loaded in one try/except that returned [] on failure, so one missing file silently disabled the entire step — including the check that already worked; (4) a spec specified `oneOf` for a constraint, but build/validate.py lists oneOf/anyOf/allOf as 'Unsupported by design', so the real gate ignores it while a jsonschema-based test goes green; (5) test stubs used `pytest.importorskip('jsonschema')`, absent from pyproject dependencies=[] and from CI, turning four assertions into silent skips that pass locally. The cheap discriminator is a negative probe: feed the gate something it MUST reject and assert a non-empty diagnostic list. Every one of these was caught that way and none by a passing suite. Corollary: `<gate> | tail -n` and `<gate>; echo $?` after a pipe report the FILTER's exit code, not the gate's — run gates unfiltered and read the real exit code.

title: A gate is not a gate until you have watched it reject something
